lines.text: Private clubs make just 13.5% from golf.
lines.say: Private clubs make just thirteen point five percent from golf.

lines.text: In 2022 data from the club managers' association, member dues brought in 49.5%.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-two data from the club managers' association, member dues brought in forty-nine point five percent.

lines.text: Food, drinks and parties added another 24.7%.
lines.say: Food, drinks and parties added another twenty-four point seven percent.

lines.text: Golf and the pro shop? Just 13.5%. Dues get paid, rain or shine.
lines.say: Golf and the pro shop? Just thirteen point five percent. Dues get paid, rain or shine.

lines.text: Public courses run on volume. Americans played a record 545 million rounds in 2024, says the National Golf Foundation.
lines.say: Public courses run on volume. Americans played a record five hundred forty-five million rounds in twenty twenty-four, says the National Golf Foundation.

lines.text: Take San Diego's city courses: $41.4 million in fiscal 2025, from 427,508 rounds.
lines.say: Take San Diego's city courses: forty-one point four million dollars in fiscal twenty twenty-five, from about four hundred twenty-eight thousand rounds.

lines.text: Our math: $41.4M / 427,508 = $96.84 a round, counting greens fees, carts, the range, the shop and food.
lines.say: Our math: that's about ninety-seven dollars a round, counting greens fees, carts, the range, the shop and food.

lines.text: So private clubs sell membership first, and public courses sell tee times by the thousand.

post.title: Private clubs make just 13.5% from golf. So what pays?
post.ig:
Private clubs make just 13.5% of their revenue from golf.
In 2022 club data from the Club Management Association of America (CMAA): dues 49.5%, food, drinks and events 24.7%, golf operations and pro shop 13.5%.
Public courses run on volume: Americans played a record 545 million rounds in 2024 (National Golf Foundation).
San Diego's city courses took in $41.4M in fiscal 2025 from 427,508 rounds. Our math: about $96.84 a round, all-in.
Sources: CMAA Board Brief (Jan/Feb 2023), National Golf Foundation, City of San Diego Golf Division (2025).
News and education, not financial advice.
